title: Retire the narrow per-file tsconfig.typetests.json projects in packages that have graduated out of TEST_DEBT
body:
Follow-up from #4040 tranche 1, filed per the PM acceptance there (2026-08-11). Unassigned — queued, not started.

## Fact

The repo carries ~10 narrow `tsconfig.typetests.json` projects that each compile ONE guard file (e.g. auth's `auth-spec-parity`, plugin-chatbot's `spec-symbol-batch6`). Their own header describes them as the rescue hatch for a package "still in TEST_DEBT" — a way to compile the load-bearing guard while the rest of the package's tests stay unchecked.

As #4040's tranches land full `tsconfig.test.json` projects, each graduated package's narrow project becomes redundant: the full project compiles the same file (verified for auth and plugin-chatbot in tranche 1 — both were left chained deliberately, since deleting a governance artifact was not that tranche's mandate).

## The ask

One PR that, for each package which has left TEST_DEBT: verifies the full test project compiles the guard file the narrow project names, then removes the narrow project and its `type-check` chain entry. Packages still in TEST_DEBT keep theirs. The `check-type-check-coverage.mjs` ratchet must stay green throughout, and the PR body lists each removed project with the proof its file is covered by the full project (a `tsc --listFiles` grep or equivalent).

Do this AFTER the #4040 burn-down has landed most packages, so it's one sweep rather than trickling — but the card exists now so it isn't lost.

## Cost of not doing it

Each redundant project is one extra tsc invocation per `type-check` run and, worse, a second project that must be kept consistent with the full one (the "two spellings of what gets compiled" shape #3009/#4040 exist to remove).

Refs #4040, #3032, objectstack-ai/objectstack#4118.
